person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the fine-grained spatial progression of best frequency through the central nucleus of the IC
span.quote: It is not known how this tonotopic pattern corresponds with the BF of single neurons, nor is it known how the stepwise progression seen by Schreiner and Langner (1997) relates to the anatomical laminae within the IC.

span.label: whether the tonotopic map in the IC is a continuous gradient or a stepwise one, and how it relates to the anatomical laminae
span.quote: The tonotopic organization in the CNIC is often assumed to be a continuous progression from low to high frequency ( Rose et al., 1966 ; Clopton and Winfield, 1973 ; Merzenich and Reid, 1974 ). However, multiunit recordings of best frequency (BF) at threshold from the CNIC in the cat have described a stepwise progression in the tonotopic organization of the IC

span.label: shows the tonotopic progression is stepwise rather than continuous, in both multiunit maps and the distribution of single-unit best frequencies, and matches the anatomical lamina thickness
span.quote: Multiunit maps demonstrate a distinct stepwise organization in the order of best frequency progression. Furthermore, independent data from single neurons show that best frequencies at octave intervals of approximately one-third are more prevalent than others.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Here, physiological and anatomical data show that best frequency is represented in a discontinuous manner in the inferior colliculus, the major auditory structure of the midbrain.

span.label: tonotopic organization in the inferior colliculus
span.quote: The present study shows a discontinuous tonotopic organization in the CNIC.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Extracellular single-unit or multiunit activity was recorded from the IC in 137 pigmented rats ( Rattus norvergicus , Rj:Long–Evans; body weight, 109–420 g) of both sexes.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: best frequencies are laid out as partially overlapping bandpass filters spaced one third of an octave apart, so near threshold the filter centre frequencies win out over the overlap regions and the measured distribution comes out saw-toothed
span.quote: Thus, near threshold, frequencies at the center of the filters are favored over those at the overlapping regions, and it results in the multi-modal, saw-toothed pattern of frequency distribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the discrete physiological frequency steps arise because the map is built from anatomically discrete fibrodendritic laminae, each lamina acting as one frequency-band module
span.quote: Thus, our anatomical and physiological data suggest that the tonotopic map in the CNIC in the rat is composed of discrete physiological laminae that correspond to the anatomical fibrodendritic laminae of the CNIC.

span.label: best frequencies are modelled as partially overlapping bandpass filters spaced a third of an octave apart, so near threshold the filter centres are favoured and produce a saw-toothed distribution
span.quote: At the IC level, best frequencies may be organized as partially overlapping bandpass filters with a center-to-center separation of one-third octave. Thus, near threshold, frequencies at the center of the filters are favored over those at the overlapping regions, and it results in the multi-modal, saw-toothed pattern of frequency distribution.

span.label: the frequency step size matches the axonal lamina thickness, about 140-150 microns
span.quote: Our data in the rat show that the axonal laminar thickness and the frequency step changes are similar across frequency (140

span.label: two to three flat neurons side by side may form the functional unit of a low-frequency lamina
span.quote: The dendritic arbors of flat cells are ∼50 μm thick and less flat cells are ∼100 μm thick on average ( Malmierca et al., 1993 , 1995 ), suggesting that two to three flat neurons organized side-by-side

span.label: electrode penetrations were angled roughly orthogonal to the isofrequency laminae so the steps would be crossed rather than followed
span.quote: Penetrations were from anterodorsal to posteroventral through the IC at an angle 10° from the frontal plane (see Fig. 8 C ). This angle is approximately orthogonal to the predominant orientation of isofrequency laminae

span.label: step size differs across structures and species and correlates with dendritic field width
span.quote: A comparison of dendritic fields suggests that the larger step size is positively correlated with a larger dendritic field width

span.label: Laminar width measurements were not corrected for histological shrinkage.
span.quote: Measurements are presented without correction for shrinkage.

span.label: The mapping of the finding onto critical bands rests on two unverified assumptions, since the number of critical bands in the rat is unknown.
span.quote: The number of critical bands in the rat is not known, but a rough estimate can be based on two assumptions: (1) the basilar membranes of mammals are scale models of each other and critical bands cover equal distances on the basilar membrane ( Greenwood, 1990 ); and (2) one critical band is thought to cover ∼1 mm (0.7–1.3 mm) on the basilar membrane.

span.label: Twelve penetrations gave no clear or incomplete tonotopic progression and were excluded from analysis.
span.quote: In 12 penetrations, no clear tonotopic organization was found ( Fig. 2 C , black symbols) or the tonotopic progression was incomplete.

span.label: steps of 50 microns or less were required to see the organisation at all, so the result depends on sampling resolution
span.quote: Electrode steps of 50 μm or less were necessary to observe the stepwise organization because the changes in frequency occurred at ∼150 μm. Previous studies ( Rose et al., 1966 ; Clopton and Winfield, 1973 ; Merzenich and Reid, 1974 ) used larger steps in their electrode mapping and thus are likely to have sampled across the stepwise organization.

span.label: most single units were collected in earlier studies with unrelated aims, in two laboratories with different equipment
span.quote: Our observations are based on two independent datasets that yielded very similar results, one from multiunit mapping and the other from single units. The multiunit mapping of the tonotopic organization was specifically collected for this study, but the single-unit data were collected in previous experiments with different aims unrelated to tonotopic organization ( Hernández et al., 2005 ; Pérez-González et al., 2005 , 2006 ). Moreover, the single-unit data were collected in two different laboratories with different sound equipment and loudspeakers. The finding of stepwise tonotopic organization using different methods suggests a robust organizational principle.

span.label: the two recording systems had different frequency ceilings, 25 kHz and 40 kHz, in a study about the distribution of best frequencies
span.quote: The maximum output of the TDT system was flat from 0.3 to 5 kHz (≈100 ± 7 dB SPL) and from 5 to 40 kHz (90 ± 5 dB SPL). The highest frequency produced by this system was limited to 40 kHz.

span.label: tonotopy here is DISCONTINUOUS by construction of the claim - a stepwise progression with a defined space of tissue per frequency band, not a smooth gradient
span.quote: Together, both types of data argue against the general view that the tonotopic organization in the CNIC forms a continuous frequency gradient. Rather, it seems that there is a defined space of collicular tissue devoted to a given frequency bandwidth.

span.label: the continuous view is named as an ASSUMPTION of the field rather than as a finding, which is what makes the paper a critique
span.quote: The resulting tonotopic map has been assumed to be a continuous smooth progression from low to high frequency throughout the central auditory system. Here, physiological and anatomical data show that best frequency is represented in a discontinuous manner in the inferior colliculus, the major auditory structure of the midbrain.

span.quote: A single previous study with multiunit recordings has shown a similar stepwise tonotopic organization in the CNIC of the cat ( Schreiner and Langner, 1997 ).

span.quote: Previous studies ( Rose et al., 1966 ; Clopton and Winfield, 1973 ; Merzenich and Reid, 1974 ) used larger steps in their electrode mapping and thus are likely to have sampled across the stepwise organization.

span.label: extends → Doron et al., 2002 (rat primary auditory cortex single units)
span.quote: To determine whether the BFs of single units in the primary auditory cortex of the rat follow a stepwise progression, we analyzed the BF of 198 cortical single units from a previous study ( Doron et al., 2002 , their Fig. 2 ) using the same approach that we used for our 604 IC single units.

span.label: contradicts → the general view that CNIC tonotopy is a continuous frequency gradient
span.quote: Together, both types of data argue against the general view that the tonotopic organization in the CNIC forms a continuous frequency gradient. Rather, it seems that there is a defined space of collicular tissue devoted to a given frequency bandwidth.

span.label: explains-away → the earlier mapping studies that reported continuity, on the grounds that they sampled too coarsely to resolve the steps
span.quote: Electrode steps of 50 μm or less were necessary to observe the stepwise organization because the changes in frequency occurred at ∼150 μm. Previous studies ( Rose et al., 1966 ; Clopton and Winfield, 1973 ; Merzenich and Reid, 1974 ) used larger steps in their electrode mapping and thus are likely to have sampled across the stepwise organization.

span.label: confirms → Schreiner and Langner's stepwise organisation in cat, at a different step size
span.quote: A single previous study with multiunit recordings has shown a similar stepwise tonotopic organization in the CNIC of the cat ( Schreiner and Langner, 1997 ). They demonstrated that frequency organization is characterized by constant-frequency ratios (on average, 0.278 octaves per frequency step) corresponding to a spatial distance of 175 μm within the IC. These steps were larger than those found in the present study of the rat, and the size differences may be related to species differences and the larger brain of the cat.

span.label: extends → Doron et al.'s cortical single-unit data, reanalysed here and found to show the same periodicity
span.quote: The cortical units showed a similar multipeaked distribution ( Fig. 9 B ), with the peaks occurring at 0.31 ± 0.10 octave intervals. The frequency distribution in the cortex is very similar to that of the distribution in the IC ( Fig. 9 B ) ( r = 0.99841). These findings suggest that there is a discontinuous tonotopic organization that begins in the IC and continues through the cortex.

span.label: supports → the proposal that critical band filters originate at the midbrain

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · stepwise —contrasted-with→ continuous
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span argued against a general view without naming either term. This sentence names both and states the contrast in eight words - 'Some appear to be CONTINUOUS, WHEREAS others are STEPWISE' - which is the cleanest contrast span merged tonight. — strength of the relation: 1 — the paper's whole claim; and note that the corpus holds both descriptions of IC tonotopy as findings, from this paper and from the studies it refutes

span.label: RETRACTED (A HEDGED CORRESPONDENCE BETWEEN TWO MEASURED RANGES, READ AS AN IDENTITY) · laminae —same-as→ critical bands
span.note: RETRACTED: A HEDGED CORRESPONDENCE BETWEEN TWO MEASURED RANGES, READ AS AN IDENTITY. The edge is `laminae --same-as--> critical bands`. The span: 'our data in the IC SUGGEST that there MAY BE 8-12 laminae, each covering 0.29-0.36 octaves. THIS SEPARATION IS SIMILAR TO critical bands of 0.333-0.375 octaves suggested for the mouse'. THREE HEDGES IN TWO SENTENCES - `suggest`, `may be`, `similar to` - and the two ranges printed are not the same range. THE SPAN STATES A RESULT ABOUT A PROPERTY AND THE EDGE ASSERTS AN IDENTITY OF THE THINGS. That is `contradicts-needs-differs-in` in mirror image: there an edge asserting disagreement dropped the parameter the disagreement turns on; here an edge asserting agreement drops the property the agreement holds for. A lamina is an anatomical structure in the inferior colliculus; a critical band is a psychoacoustic construct. What is similar is their WIDTH IN OCTAVES, which is the property the edge drops. — strength of the relation: 0.7 — hedged and argued from two independent counts agreeing at 8-12; a psychoacoustic construct identified with an anatomical one
span.quote: Interestingly, our data in the IC suggest that there may be 8–12 laminae, each covering 0.29–0.36 octaves. This separation is similar to critical bands of 0.333–0.375 octaves suggested for the mouse

span.quote: These midbrain bandpass filters have broader bandwidth than those conceived at the periphery to model the output of the cochlea ( Moore, 1986 ; Moore et al., 1999 ; Moore and Glasberg, 2007 ). If the auditory filters in the rat are similar, the midbrain filters may be approximately double those at the periphery.
